History: Aramean kingdoms, chiefly Damascus, rose after the Bronze Age collapse and contested the land east and north of Israel. Aram fought Israel under Ben-Hadad and Hazael, allied with it at times, and finally fell to Assyria in 732 BC.
Culture: Aramaic, the language of the Arameans, became the lingua franca of the Near East and the everyday language of Jesus' world. Aramean trade and diplomacy connected Mesopotamia with the Levant.
Religion: Arameans worshipped Hadad (Rimmon), the storm god, among others. Naaman, commander of Aram's army, was healed of leprosy after washing in the Jordan at Elisha's word.
BibleConnection: Aram is both enemy and neighbor in Kings: wars with Ahab and Jehoram, the siege of Samaria, and Naaman's healing, which showed God's mercy reaching beyond Israel.
